subject: Request: on-prem / physical-hosting variance + audit schedule
messages:
From: Lucia Moreno <procurement@aureliahealth.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosting request: on-site/private deployment & audit schedule

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the demo last week — Aurelia is excited about Redwood's latency profile. Our security and operations teams have one important constraint: we need the initial pilot to run on physical hardware hosted inside our NYC data center (private, customer-managed colo) to satisfy state regulator requirements for PHI processing.

Key asks from procurement/security:
- Data residency: customer-only storage in our NYC footprint; no backups outside region.
- Audit rights: monthly audit window (on-site), 24-hour engineer access during audit, and exportable system logs for the audit period.
- Deployment constraints: dedicated single-tenant host(s) for pilot; limited remote support until onboarding is complete.
- Commercial: we can commit to a 12-month pilot with a 4-node reserved footprint. That commitment is contingent on a 25% credit on list hosting fees and inclusion of the monthly audit window in the agreement.

I've attached a draft SOW that includes the scope and our preferred language. Can your team route this for pricing + legal approval and let us know what exceptions Redwood can accept?

Tom Beller (ops) is copied to help with technical details.

Thanks,
Lucia Moreno
Procurement Manager
Aurelia Health

Attachment: Aurelia_SOW_draft.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Lucia Moreno <procurement@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosting request: on-site/private deployment & audit schedule

Hi Lucia — thanks for the clear summary and the SOW. I’ve looped in Markus (Deal Desk) and Laura (Legal) to coordinate commercial and contract language.

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) Deal desk to confirm whether we can offer a one-time "physical hosting" setup with a discounted pilot rate and list the engineering hours required.
2) Legal to propose narrower audit language so we can balance regulator needs and Redwood’s operational security.
3) Engineering sync with Tom to confirm what on-site access/support will look like during the pilot.

Markus/Laura — can you confirm what level of discount and audit carveouts are feasible, and whether we need exec approval for this concession? I’ll schedule a short sync with Aurelia if helpful.

Irene Choi
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosting request: on-site/private deployment & audit schedule

Irene — thanks, added to deal desk queue. Summary of commercial view:
- Customer asks: 25% credit on hosting fees for 12-mo pilot + monthly on-site audit windows and dedicated hardware.
- Risk/cost drivers: dedicated physical hosting + increased eng & ops support during audits. Estimated incremental cost: $85K in onboarding + ~$6K/month ops overhead.

Proposed commercial concession for exec consideration:
- Approve up to 20% credit on hosting fees for the 12-month pilot (not to exceed $120K total concession).
- Audit access: convert monthly on-site audits to quarterly on-site audits with a maximum 72-hour notice and a documented checklist; allow one "emergency" on-site audit per year with 24-hour notice and sign-off from Redwood Security.
- Engineering time beyond the standard onboarding (estimated 160 hours) to be billable at our professional services rates unless we agree to a capped onboarding credit ($40K max).

Irene, please ask the customer whether they can accept quarterly audits with limited emergency access. If not, we will need exec approval for the original monthly request and the larger concession.

Requesting Ben for explicit executive approval or direction on the upper bound of concession we can make here.

-Markus

Attachment: SOW_redline_v1.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 14:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosting request: on-site/private deployment & audit schedule

Team — reviewed the SOW and Aurelia's ask. Legal concerns and suggested alternatives:

1) Audit rights: monthly on-site with 24-hour engineer access is excessive from a contractual and security perspective. Proposed language: customer may request quarterly on-site audits supported by a formal audit plan; Redwood will provide relevant exportable logs and a SOC 2 Type II report covering the audit period. On-site, hands-on access to systems will require a subpoena or regulatory order unless otherwise agreed in a separate statement of work with explicit escort and limited scope.

2) Data residency: we can accept customer-only residency in their region for the pilot provided host-level snapshots, backups, and disaster recovery copies are explicitly scheduled within region and not replicated across regions. Add a cross-reference to our data-handling appendix and KMS control procedures.

3) HSM/KMS: if Aurelia requires customer-managed keys/HSM in their colo, we need to confirm supported integrations. This will likely require additional SRE work and a 4–6 week lead time. Include that as billable work or a separate milestone in the SOW.

If the customer insists on monthly on-site access, escalate to execs with a clear cost/ops impact and proposed mitigations.

-Laura Bennett
General Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosting request: on-site/private deployment & audit schedule

Markus / Laura / Irene — I’ve reviewed the ask and legal's notes. Executive position and conditional approval:

- Commercial concession: approve up to 15% credit on hosting fees for the 12-month pilot, provided Aurelia signs the SOW with the following constraints: (a) audit frequency limited to quarterly on-site audits with a documented checklist; (b) any additional on-site access beyond quarterly requires a paid professional-services engagement and 14-day notice; (c) the total concession cap will be $80K.
- Engineering: cap onboarding credit to $40K; any hours beyond the estimate will be invoiced.
- Data residency & KMS: agree to region-only storage and will evaluate customer-managed KMS integration as a separate SOW (estimated 4–6 weeks).

This is approval to proceed to customer with the above compromise. If Aurelia cannot accept quarterly audits (and insists on monthly 24-hour access), escalate to CEO for a final decision.

Ben Carter
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Lucia Moreno <procurement@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Tom Beller <tom.beller@aureliahealth.com>, markus.klein@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosting request: on-site/private deployment & audit schedule

Hi Lucia / Tom — thank you for the SOW and clarity on requirements. Good news: leadership has approved a constrained path forward. Summary of approved items and conditions (please review):

1) Commercial: Redwood will offer a 15% credit on hosting fees for the 12-month pilot (capped at $80K).
2) Audit schedule: quarterly on-site audits (one per quarter) with a documented audit checklist. We will support one additional "emergency" on-site audit per 12-month period with 14 days' notice; emergency access will require a separate paid engagement.
3) Engineering & onboarding: we will provide an onboarding credit up to $40K; any hours beyond the agreed estimate will be billed per our PS rates.
4) Data residency: production data and backups will remain within the NYC footprint for the pilot. Any replication outside the region is prohibited unless explicitly listed in the SOW.
5) KMS/HSM: Redwood will evaluate customer-managed KMS integration as a separate project with an estimated 4–6 week lead time; we will not delay pilot start for that work.

Next steps:
- I’ve attached a redlined SOW for your review (SOW_redline_v1.pdf).
- If Aurelia accepts the redlines, we will send the final SOW + DocuSign link for signature (DocuSign link included below).
